summary: Redwood walked Zenith Ops through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for latency-sensitive inference; security (SOC2/KMS/SAML) and cost per route are primary decision factors. Agreed next steps include pricing, security docs, and a pilot benchmark.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start time: 09:23 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Evan Marshall (Redwood AE), Priya Kaur (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (CTO, Zenith Ops), Aisha Rahman (Head of ML Ops), Marco Diaz (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): walked through the console usage analytics, per route dashboards, and cost breakdown. customer asked about dedicated capacity and security docs. agreed to run a pilot and share pricing.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood — joining me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Liam: Good, thanks. Excited to see the console stuff — we've been looking at per-route costs a lot lately.
[00:12] Priya: Awesome. Today's agenda: quick context check, then console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, tagging, and then the cost breakdown section and how optimize recommendations show up. We'll leave 10 minutes for Q&A and next steps.
[00:25] Aisha: Sounds good. For context, we run a mix of hosted endpoints and some on-prem for PHI workloads. Looking to consolidate where possible. latency is a hard constraint for our chat product.
[00:36] Evan: Perfect, that's helpful. Priya, can you share screen?
[00:40] Priya: Yep sharing now — tell me if the screen is blurry. Okay, so this is the Redwood Console home. Top-level is usage over time, token counts, and per-route breakdown. You can filter by model, route, and deployment type — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[01:05] Priya: Here on the left we have routes — you can tag routes by team, environment, and cost-center. I'm clicking into our sample route "chat-support-441". You'll see request distribution, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:20] Marco: Quick Q — are those cost numbers live tied to the actual per-GPU run rates, or are they just estimates?
[01:28] Priya: They're driven by your configured pricing profile; for hosted customers we populate default unit costs, but for Dedicated or Private you can plug in your committed rates or cloud GPU costs. It's intended to reconcile with your bill. It's not a bill itself, it's a unit economics view.
[01:45] Liam: Nice. Can I break down cost by prompt vs completion tokens?
[01:50] Priya: Yep — toggle shows prompt vs completion and also shows KV cache hits so you can see how prefix caching reduces token counts. Note: the transcript on this screen shows "KV cash" in some older exports — ignore that small OCR thing — actual metric is KV cache hit rate.
[02:10] Evan: We often see customers surprised by hidden cost drivers — long contexts, embedding reranks, or high frequency low-value calls. The per-route dashboards help you find those.
[02:22] Aisha: That's actually our pain point — we have a lot of tiny routes doing semantic search and the unit costs add up. We want to see which ones to bundle or cache.
[02:30] Priya: Exactly, you can sort routes by cost per 1000 tokens, or cost per successful response, and then create rules to route those queries to quantized model variants or batch them.
[02:43] Marco: Does the console recommend quantization profiles?
[02:46] Priya: Yes, under Optimize -> Model Suggestions we show recommended quantization and batching configs based on historical latency/quality tradeoffs. It will flag routes with high cost and low latency sensitivity and recommend 4-bit or int8 profiles.
[03:02] Liam: I'm assuming there's a way to see the real-time cost as we change batching? Like if I bump max_batch to 8 what happens?
[03:08] Priya: There's a sandbox simulation — run a hypothetical config and it will project token/sec and cost delta based on your traffic distribution. We can run that in the pilot.
[03:18] Evan: Jumping to the per-route dashboard, here's an example of an A/B rollout. You can pin a model version per route and define fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity is saturated it fails over to a hosted variant or a lower-cost quantized variant.
[03:33] Aisha: Does the failover preserve KV cache? We're worried about thrashing and cold starts.
[03:39] Priya: Good question. If the fallback is to a compatible model family and you've set cache replication, we replicate prefix cache across variants. If you fall back to a different architecture you will lose the KV cache. We call that out in the rollout UI.
[03:55] Marco: Security — where do we see audit logs and who accessed what route?
[03:59] Priya: Under Observability -> Audit logs. You can export logs to your SIEM and we have event types for model deploys, route changes, and token-level request traces. For Private deployments we support customer-side KMS/HSM integration so we don't see plaintext keys.
[04:15] Liam: Do you offer SSO/SAML and RBAC? We need role-based access controls aligned with internal roles.
[04:20] Evan: Yes SSO/SAML is available, and RBAC is part of the console — roles like view-only, deployer, admin. We also integrate with SCIM for provisioning.
[04:30] Aisha: Also need SOC2 and ISO attestation for procurement.
[04:33] Evan: We'll send the SOC2 pack and deployment hardening docs after — that's one of the next steps.
[04:40] Priya: Back to cost breakdown: here's a route-level timeline showing token volume, cost, latency, and a breakdown by model variant. See that spike at ~10/22? You can click into the session trace and see prompt length distribution and which user flows drove it.
[04:57] Priya: One nuance — our cost calc includes GPU execution time and extrapolated infra egress and storage costs; customers can toggle which components to include.
[05:10] Marco: For Dedicated, if we commit to reserved capacity, how granular is the reporting — per-gpu vs per-customer?
[05:16] Priya: Dedicated reporting shows pool utilization, per-tenant throughput, and per-route consumption. You can get per-GPU traces if you want to do low-level profiling.
[05:27] Liam: What about private on-prem? Can we send metrics to our internal prometheus?
[05:32] Priya: Yes, Private has exporters; you can push to Prometheus or pull logs into Datadog.
[05:38] Evan: Let's demo a quick cost drilldown on a heavy route — "quicksearch-prod".
[05:43] Priya: Opening it now — you'll see the top contributors: long prompt templates, high completion tokens, and a rerank job that runs every query. If you enable prefix caching and switch rerank to a batched async job we estimate a 36% cost reduction.
[06:02] Aisha: How do you estimate quality impact when you quantize? We can't afford regression on NLU.
[06:08] Priya: We link quantization recommendations to historical evals in the console. For each route we show a small sample of prompts and outputs pre/post quantization and a delta metric (BLEU/ROUGE or custom evals you upload). You can also run canary rollouts to 1% of traffic and monitor quality regressions.
[06:26] Marco: Is the canary automatic rollback if metrics degrade?
[06:29] Priya: Yes you can set thresholds and automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions.
[06:33] Evan: Quick aside on economics — some customers use Optimize to set cost SLOs per route, e.g., max $0.10 per successful response, and the system will route to cheaper variants or cache accordingly.
[06:47] Liam: We may want that — we need per-customer SLA enforcement.
[06:50] Priya: We have per-route policies and per-tenant budgets that can trigger throttling or re-routing.
[06:57] Aisha: Ok show me the exports — can we get a CSV with daily per-route costs for the last 90 days?
[07:03] Priya: Yes, export -> daily cost by route. You can schedule exports to S3. For Private, we'll give you an S3-compatible endpoint.
[07:12] Liam: On the security side, for Private, how does key management work? We want envelope encryption and HSM.
[07:18] Evan: Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS; we support envelope encryption patterns and optional HSM integration. Keys never leave customer control.
[07:27] Marco: Any compliance for audit trail? Retention windows?
[07:30] Priya: Audit logs retention is configurable; for Hosted we have default retention tiers and longer retention is an add-on. For Dedicated you can set retention in the console and export to your archive.
[07:41] Evan: Let's switch to a live simulation: I'm going to toggle a route to use quantized 4-bit variant and simulate running your traffic for 48 hours. Priya, can you run the sim?
[07:48] Priya: Running now — projection shows 28% cost savings for that route at 4-bit with p95 latency increasing by 12ms, still within your 250ms SLO.
[08:01] Liam: That's promising. Any caveats?
[08:03] Priya: Quality deltas are shown in the linked eval. For this route we see minor freshness in longer completions but high accuracy for classification tasks.
[08:13] Aisha: How do we pin this change in production? We need staged rollout and stakeholders sign-off.
[08:18] Priya: The console lets you create an approval flow — deploy to canary, wait for sign-off, then promote. Sign-offs can map to Slack or email.
[08:27] Evan: Back to economics — we also show a per-route amortized Dedicated cost when you have reserved capacity. It spreads cluster cost across routes by actual usage so you can see true marginal cost.
[08:40] Marco: If we want to run a pilot, what's the minimal setup?
[08:44] Evan: Minimal pilot is a 2-week benchmark: you provide traffic sample or replay, we run it against a dedicated pool or hosted config, measure latency and cost, and we'll run the Optimize recommendations. Priya will own the runbook.
[08:56] Priya: I'll draft the benchmark runbook and share. We'll need a traffic sample and 2-3 representative routes.
[09:04] Liam: Who will run the tests? Do you need VPN or access to our VPC?
[09:09] Priya: For hosted we just need traffic sample and we simulate; for Private or Dedicated inside your VPC we'd coordinate secure access — typically an SSH bastion + limited ingress and we can deploy the private agent. We'll share an ops checklist.
[09:23] Evan: Ok I want to call out the things procurement will ask — pricing, SOC2, contract terms, and data residency. We'll send a templated pricing deck and procurement sheet.
[09:34] Aisha: On pricing, can you give a ballpark now for reserved Dedicated?
[09:38] Evan: Ballpark depends on commit level; I'll send tiered pricing. For context, many customers see 20-40% cost reduction using Optimize and dedicated pooling vs naive hosted at scale, but results vary.
[09:50] Marco: Any customers in healthcare doing PHI workloads? We need references.
[09:54] Evan: We can share sanitized references and case studies. We'll include that in the packet.
[09:59] Priya: Quick note — sometimes transcription shows product names wrong (like Redwood Dedicate) — ignore that in the exported notes.
[10:07] Aisha: (laughs) noted.
[10:10] Evan: Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[10:13] Evan: Action items: Evan to send pricing and SOC2; Priya to prepare benchmark runbook and per-route dashboard template; Liam to send traffic sample and desired SLAs; schedule a pilot kickoff next week if possible.
[10:25] Liam: Sounds good, target sending sample by Friday.
[10:28] Aisha: We'll sync internally and confirm stakeholders.
[10:31] Marco: If you can include a short how-to for setting up KMS + HSM that would help.
[10:36] Priya: Will include that.
[10:38] Evan: Anything else?
[10:40] Liam: One last quick question — does your console surface per-user cost for multi-tenant customers?
[10:45] Priya: You can slice by tenant ID if you instrument requests and include tenant metadata; we show tenant-level chargebacks.
[10:53] Evan: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet.
[10:58] Aisha: Thanks Evan, Priya.
[11:00] Marco: Thanks.
[11:02] Evan: Bye all.

Post-call notes: follow up with pricing deck, SOC2 & deployment security docs, benchmark runbook, and sample per-route dashboard. Customer to provide traffic sample and SLA targets.
